items.titulo: Cellular scaling laws in the mammalian brain
items.resumen: This perspective argues that our brains do not operate as a single system; instead, there are two systems, where one is a copy-paste “learning” engine that scales by duplicating the same modules and the other is a bespoke “steering” system that scales by inventing entirely new cell types for every drive and reflex. This split between systems could reshape how we treat addiction and depression and how we build AI.
